You said:You

use Redux for state management whats this

ChatGPT said:ChatGPT

Redux is a state management library for React. It helps your application manage and share data between different components without having to pass information manually from one component to another.

For your J&J K-POP Merchandise Online Store, Redux can help manage things like:

  • Shopping cart items

  • Product information

  • Customer authentication

  • Logged-in user information

  • Order information

  • Wishlist items

1. What problem does Redux solve?

Imagine your store has these pages:

  • Home

  • Products

  • Product Details

  • Shopping Cart

  • Checkout

  • My Profile

A customer adds an album to their cart on the Products page.

When they open the Shopping Cart page, the added album should still be there.

Without centralized state management, you might need to pass cart information between several components or implement separate state logic.

Redux solves this by providing a centralized store.

Redux Store Architecture

Redux Store

Centralized application state

Cart
User
Products
Orders

Home Page

Products Page

Cart Page

Checkout Page

All these components can access and update shared application state through Redux.

2. Example in your shopping cart

Suppose a customer adds three K-pop albums.

Shopping Cart

K-pop Album A

Quantity: 2

₱1,000

Photocard Set

Quantity: 1

₱250

Total

₱1,250

Illustrative shopping cart

Redux keeps track of the cart data, so the Cart and Checkout components can access the same information.

3. How to implement Redux in React

I recommend using Redux Toolkit, the official recommended approach for writing Redux logic.

Step 1. Install Redux

In your React frontend terminal:

Bash
npm install @reduxjs/toolkit react-redux

Step 2. Create a Redux store

Create:

src/redux/store.js

JavaScript
import { configureStore } from "@reduxjs/toolkit";
import cartReducer from "./cartSlice";

export const store = configureStore({
    reducer: {
        cart: cartReducer
    }
});

Step 3. Create a cart slice

Create:

src/redux/cartSlice.js

JavaScript
import { createSlice } from "@reduxjs/toolkit";

const cartSlice = createSlice({
    name: "cart",

    initialState: {
        items: []
    },

    reducers: {
        addToCart: (state, action) => {
            state.items.push(action.payload);
        },

        clearCart: (state) => {
            state.items = [];
        }
    }
});

export const { addToCart, clearCart } =
    cartSlice.actions;

export default cartSlice.reducer;

Step 4. Connect Redux to React

In src/main.jsx:

JavaScript
import { Provider } from "react-redux";
import { store } from "./redux/store";

<Provider store={store}>
    <App />
</Provider>

Keep your existing React rendering code inside the Provider.

Step 5. Use Redux in your components

For example, in your Product component:

JavaScript
import { useDispatch } from "react-redux";
import { addToCart } from "../redux/cartSlice";

function Product({ product }) {

    const dispatch = useDispatch();

    const handleAddToCart = () => {
        dispatch(addToCart(product));
    };

    return (
        <button onClick={handleAddToCart}>
            Add to Cart
        </button>
    );
}

Now your Product component can add products to the centralized Redux store.

4. Which parts of your project should use Redux?

Feature

Use Redux?

Shopping cart

Yes

Logged-in user information

Yes

Authentication state

Yes

Product listings

Optional

Wishlist

Yes

Checkout information

Optional

Admin order management

Optional

Important: Redux is not your database. MongoDB still stores permanent information. Redux manages application state on the frontend.

For example, a Redux cart can be cleared when the page refreshes unless you implement persistence. You can use Redux Persist or your backend to preserve cart data.

5. What does your instructor expect?

If your requirement says "Use Redux for state management," you should be able to demonstrate:

  1. Redux Toolkit is installed.

  2. A Redux store is created.

  3. Your React application is connected using Provider.

  4. You have at least one slice, such as cartSlice.

  5. Components use useDispatch() to update state.

  6. Components use useSelector() to retrieve state.

My recommendation

Start by implementing Redux for your shopping cart. This is the easiest and most practical feature to demonstrate in your J&J K-POP store.

You can then extend it to authentication and user information.

what do you suggest about reviewign a product. for example i ordered 2 different products, their reviews should be separate right?

ChatGPT said:ChatGPT

Yes! Each product should have its own separate review, even if both products were purchased in the same order.

For your J&J K-POP Merchandise Online Store, I recommend implementing a per-product review system rather than one review per order.

1. Example scenario

Suppose a customer purchases two different products in one order:

Order #10025

K-pop Album

₱1,200 · Qty: 1

Completed

Photocard Set

₱250 · Qty: 1

Completed

Your reviews

K-pop Album

Not reviewed

Photocard Set

Reviewed

★★★★★

5/5

The customer can review the album without reviewing the photocard set.

2. Recommended review rules

Rule

Recommended behavior

Review per product

Separate reviews

Multiple products in one order

Each can be reviewed independently

Eligibility

Only purchased products from completed orders

Duplicate reviews

One review per customer per product per order

Edit review

Allowed once

After editing

Permanently locked

Delete review

Not allowed, if following your one-time edit policy

Rating

1–5 stars

Comment

Optional or required, depending on your preference

Important: I recommend one review per customer per product per order. This means if a customer buys the same product again in a different order, they can submit another review for that purchase.

3. Recommended MongoDB review structure

For example:

JavaScript
{
    user: ObjectId("USER_ID"),
    product: ObjectId("PRODUCT_ID"),
    order: ObjectId("ORDER_ID"),

    rating: 5,
    comment: "The album arrived safely!",

    editCount: 0,

    createdAt: Date,
    updatedAt: Date
}

You can use these three IDs to identify exactly who reviewed which product from which order.

4. How the review system should work

Review workflow

  1. Customer places an order containing multiple products.
  2. Admin marks the order as Completed.
  3. Each purchased product gets its own review option.
  4. Customer submits an individual rating and comment.
  5. Customer can edit that specific review once.
  6. After the edit, that review becomes locked.

5. One additional recommendation

If a customer purchases two quantities of the same product in one order, they should still submit only one review for that product in that order, not two separate reviews.

This prevents duplicate reviews and inflated product ratings.

My final recommendation: Use a product-based review system linked to the customer and order. This is more organized, prevents duplicate reviews, and ensures customers only review products they actually purchased.
